02What I’ve Built and Tested

Four ways I’ve turned questions into systems I could build, test, and ship.

Ideas become more interesting to me when I can build something around them, put them in front of evidence, and find out where I was wrong.

Research System

CounterRefine

TESTED

AI can find relevant evidence and still give the wrong answer.

I designed, implemented, and evaluated CounterRefine, a system that checks an AI’s first answer against additional evidence and decides whether to keep or revise it. The goal is more reliable factual answers without changing answers unnecessarily.

  1. 01Start with an answer
  2. 02Search to check it
  3. 03Keep or revise
  4. 04Check the revision

Did it work beyond this example?

GPT-5
67.3% → 73.1%
+5.8 percentage points
Claude Sonnet 4.6
63.7% → 67.7%
+4.0 percentage points

Accuracy on all 4,326 factual questions in SimpleQA. Each comparison uses the same model’s matched baseline: one retrieval-and-answer pass (one-pass RAG).

A correction can also introduce an error.In the full Claude evaluation, CounterRefine changed 5.6% of outputs. There were 180 changes from incorrect to correct and 8 from correct to incorrect; other changes did not alter correctness.

Emotional Reflection Tool
SHIPPED

FocusPal

Helping people understand why they are stuck, then take a first step.

I built and published FocusPal, a Chrome extension for moments when someone wants to work but cannot begin. Instead of starting with a timer, I designed a guided reflection that connects emotions, underlying beliefs, and a small next action.

How the product works

Example interaction from the product overview

  1. Recognize the barrier“I need to work, but I just can’t start.”
  2. Examine the belief“If I cannot do this perfectly, it means I am inadequate.”
  3. Find a gentler next stepConsider: “I am enough, even when I’m still learning.” Then choose: “Open the document and write one sentence.”

User-tested

Four approaches behind the design

ACTAcceptance and Commitment Therapy

Notice a difficult thought without automatically treating it as a fact or an instruction.

Self-Compassion

Respond to struggle with kindness rather than adding self-criticism.

Ho’oponopono

A reconciliation practice that informs prompts for forgiveness and letting go.

Zen Mindfulness

Bring attention back to present thoughts and feelings without immediately judging them.

Solo Study

Human–AI Interaction

COMPLETED

Same AI. Different ways of working together.

I independently designed and ran a study with 15 high school students to compare coding-task performance across three GPT-4o interaction styles.

On requestWaits for the student to ask
ProactiveOffers suggestions unprompted
CollaborativeWorks through dialogue

What I measured: task-completion time, submitted code, and participant feedback.

OBSERVED RESULT

The collaborative condition had the shortest average completion time in this study.

NEXT BUILD → HELPDIAL

Does the benefit carry over when AI is gone?

This study measured performance with AI. HelpDial adds a delayed task without AI to investigate independent learning.

Behavioral Research System

Modeling Procrastination

DEPLOYED

I built a way to study hesitation as decisions unfold.

Surveys capture what students remember about their habits. I wanted to examine choices during a simulated academic project, so I independently built an interactive research tool and used it with 66 high school students.

Try the simulation ↗Download research poster ↓
Meaningful choices. Shared checkpoints.

The 14-node narrative introduces ambiguity, distraction, uneven workloads, and time pressure. Branching paths reconverge at predefined checkpoints, allowing different choices within a comparable research structure.

Built for data collection

The system automatically records choices, timestamps, and predefined score updates, then exports structured data for analysis.

FROM RESEARCH TO FOCUSPAL

The study informed my next build: FocusPal, a Chrome extension designed to help people understand what is blocking them and choose a manageable next step.

Reading the results

The analysis traced cumulative decision patterns within the simulation. Scores follow predefined rules and are not a diagnosis or a validated prediction of real-world performance.

Built independently, end to endNarrative design · System implementation · Data collection & analysis

Outside the Lab

Teaching World War II in Rural China

At a rural boarding school in China, I taught World War II with prepared lectures, videos, and explanations.

The classroom became more engaged when students began building models, debating choices, and making decisions themselves.

Those moments drew my attention to the space a lesson leaves for students to think and participate.

03WHAT I’M BUILDING NOW
INDEPENDENT PROJECT · IN DEVELOPMENT

HelpDial

Who controls how much an AI tutor reveals?

I’m developing HelpDial, an AI statistics tutor that recommends a level of help and explains why. Students can accept the recommendation, choose a different level, or flag a misunderstanding of their reasoning.

$5,000
School STEM GrantResearch funding awarded to support HelpDial

Enough support to move forward. Room to reason.

Giving away a solution can replace a student’s thinking. Withholding help can leave them stuck. HelpDial makes the amount of assistance an explicit decision students can inspect and change.

See why

See the recommended help level and an explanation based on the work shown.

Choose how much

Select from five levels, from a guiding question to a full worked explanation.

Correct a misunderstanding

Tell the tutor when it has misread your reasoning before continuing.

Does the help carry over when AI is gone?

The planned randomized study compares ordinary AI tutoring, system-controlled help, and help students can inspect and adjust.

3 statistics tasksWith AI tutoring
48–96 hours later →
6 transfer questionsWithout AI assistance

What the study will measure

Primary outcome: six delayed questions completed without AI, scored by two graders who do not know each student’s assigned condition.

During tutoring: track whether the AI reveals reasoning too early, whether the student first articulates key reasoning steps, and how much control students feel they have.

Study topics: hypothesis testing, confidence intervals, and causal inference. The visible recommendations and student controls are evaluated together as one interface condition.

Current progress

Research plan, task bank, and participant materials prepared. Recruitment and data collection have not begun.

What makes us trust an answer?

Through essays and two independently published books, I examine how we judge information, what models can explain about people, and how interacting with AI may change us.

MARSHALL SOCIETY · 2025 SHORTLIST

To What Extent Can Mathematical Modelling Capture the Complexity of Human Behavior?

A prediction can change the behavior it tries to predict. I distinguish three layers of behavior: stable incentives, adaptation to predictions, and choices shaped by identity. Each reveals a different limit of mathematical modelling.

Objectivity Is a Feeling: Reframing Truth as Trust

An AI’s conversational style can change how credible the same information feels. Drawing on my human–AI interaction experiment, I argue that our sense of objectivity depends partly on how information reaches us, not just what it says.
